questions.question:
Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D.

Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

The Ramayana is one of the largest ancient

A. 24,000 verses divided into seven Khanda (parts)

B. the first and the seventh being later additions.

C. epics in world literature. It consists of nearly

D. It belongs to the genre of Itihasa, narratives of past events, interspersed with teachings on the goals of human life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct sequence** to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence is **CABD.**
 
• **C. **"The Ramayana is one of the largest ancient epics in world literature." **This part sets up the topic **of the sentence, which is the Ramayana.
 
• **A.** "It consists of nearly 24,000 verses divided into seven Khanda (parts)" **This provides specific details **about the structure of the Ramayana, following logically from the introduction of the Ramayana as the topic.
 
• **B.** "the first and the seventh being later additions." **This provides additional detail** about the structure of the Ramayana, specifically the first and seventh parts.
 
• **D. **"It belongs to the genre of Itihasa, narratives of past events, interspersed with teachings on the goals of human life." This is a general statement about the Ramayana's genre and thematic content, which serves as a suitable conclusion to the sentence.

Therefore, the **correct and meaningful sentence** is: *"The Ramayana is one of the largest ancient epics in world literature. It consists of nearly 24,000 verses divided into seven Khanda (parts), the first and the seventh being later additions. It belongs to the genre of Itihasa, narratives of past events, interspersed with teachings on the goals of human life."*

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The actors __is to shoot__ the scene three times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'** i.e.** 'Had to shoot'.**

__
 
• The** sentence** "The actors is to shoot the scene three times." is** incorrect** due to the** verb agreement error.**
 
• The verb **"is" **should be r**eplaced by "had"** to agree with the plural subject and given options. 
 
• **"had to shoot"** - The sentence would then read: "The actors had to shoot the scene three times."
 
• **This suggests **that the actors were required to shoot the scene three times in the past.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: '*The actors had to shoot the scene three times.'*

• **"had to shooting" **- This option is grammatically incorrect. The correct form after "had to" is the base form of the verb, so it should be "shoot," not "shooting".
 
• **"has to shoot"** - This form would be correct if the subject was singular (like "The actor"), but since the subject is plural ("The actors"), the correct verb form would be "have to shoot," not "has to shoot".

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.

“Who is it?” Vikram asked, his euphoria fading.

options.text: With a faded euphoria Vikram asked who is it.
As his euphoria faded, Vikram asks as to who was it.
With his euphoria faded, Vikram asked who it is.
With his euphoria fading, Vikram asked who it was.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4' .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In indirect speech, we often change the tense of the verb back one step in** 'time'.**
 
• This is known as **'backshifting'.** Hence, the present tense "is" changes to the past tense "was".
 
• The noun **"Vikram"** **remains **the same as it is a proper noun, and the pronoun **"it"** remains the same because it's an object pronoun that doesn't need to change when the speech becomes indirect.
 
• Also, **in this sentenc**e, "With his euphoria fading" is a **perfect translation **of "his euphoria fading" that allows for smoother sentence flow and better readability.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'With his euphoria fading, Vikram asked who it was.'*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Ravish likes chocolate.

options.text: Chocolate is being liked by Ravish.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the original sentence,** "likes"** is in the **simple present **tense, so **we need to maintain** the same tense in the passive voice.
 
• **When changing **a sentence from active to passive voice, the **object** of the active sentence (here "chocolate")** becomes the subject** of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb **'like'** **changes **to **'is liked'** to match the tense and the passive structure.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: '*Chocolate is liked by Ravish.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"Chocolate was liked by Ravish." **- This uses the past tense ("was liked"), which changes the original tense of the sentence.
 
• **"Chocolate were liked by Ravish." **- This is grammatically incorrect because "were liked" should be used with plural subjects, and "chocolate" is singular.
 
• **"Chocolate is being liked by Ravish." **- The phrase "is being liked" suggests an ongoing action, which changes the tense and the meaning of the original sentence. "Like" is also a stative verb, which doesn't usually use continuous (progressive) tenses.
